question: Who sent the unexpected SIGTERM caught during attempt 3, and why?

findings.worker_code: The only in-worker timer is signal.setitimer(ITIMER_REAL, remaining_campaign_seconds), which is intended to raise SIGALRM at the recorded absolute campaign deadline. A separate SIGTERM handler labels a received SIGTERM as a generic campaign-manager stop; it does not identify the sender. No subprocess timeout=, signal.alarm, or shell timeout wrapper is present in the resume worker or the VUMPS/half-row solver.
findings.process_wrapper: The observed start_process run.cmd contains only the env assignments and python command; the process metadata records name, command, working directory, and startedAt, with no runtime timeout. start_process was called with startup_wait=5 seconds; this is startup waiting, not a runtime cap.
findings.process_limits: At observation, /proc/2925/limits showed unlimited CPU time, resident set, data size, and address space. The worker used one thread and about 110608 KiB RSS. Its cgroup path was /user; available root cpu.stat had nr_throttled=0 and throttled_usec=0; no memory.max or memory.events file was exposed at the mounted cgroup root. This does not show an OOM or CPU-quota cause.
findings.kernel_and_journal: dmesg and journalctl -k searches over the relevant window returned no OOM, killed-process, quota/throttling, or SIGTERM entries. The sandbox does not expose a signal-audit record containing the sender PID.
findings.process_manager_records: The attempt-3 process-manager directory/log was no longer available when checked. The active attempt-4 metadata had no runtime timeout field. get_process_output had returned not_found for the earlier handle, but this did not identify the signal sender.
findings.behavioral_test: Attempt 3 is the only recorded unexpected SIGTERM. The next worker (attempt 4) passed cumulative iteration 9 and reached iteration 16; it therefore was not killed at a deterministic 9–10-iteration threshold. No run outside the Arena process supervisor is available from these tools.
findings.intentional_pause: After the user asked to investigate before further compute, I intentionally invoked stop_process on attempt 4. The worker caught that requested SIGTERM, wrote the iteration-16 checkpoint, and exited. This deliberate pause is known and distinct from the earlier unexplained SIGTERM.

result: The earlier SIGTERM sender/cause cannot be identified from the available sandbox logs. The agent worker has no short runtime timeout, and the available evidence does not implicate OOM or CPU throttling. A host/process-supervisor signal remains possible but unproven.
status: unresolved; compute held pending signal-source identification or external supervisor logs
